PF1MK.Settings.PlayerButton.Name: Knowledge roll chat button
PF1MK.Settings.PlayerButton.Hint: Adds a monster-question button to Knowledge skill roll chat messages.
PF1MK.Settings.GMButton.Name: GM token-control button
PF1MK.Settings.GMButton.Hint: Adds a GM-only token control button. It uses controlled tokens.
PF1MK.Settings.InfoSelection.Name: Information selection interface
PF1MK.Settings.InfoSelection.Hint: If enabled, players can spend questions on information categories. If disabled, the module only posts the question count.
PF1MK.Settings.SimplifiedQuestions.Name: Simplified questions
PF1MK.Settings.SimplifiedQuestions.Hint: Combines some questions: AC includes normal, touch, and flat-footed AC; energy resistance includes damage immunities and numbered energy resistance; saves include all saving throws; movement speed includes the main speeds.
PF1MK.Settings.HideSharedFeatureHiddenTe: If enabled, hidden, secret, and GM-only text blocks are not shown when opening a shared feature from chat. If disabled, the module reveals them as before.
PF1MK.Settings.FeatureMode.Name: Special features mode
PF1MK.Settings.FeatureMode.Hint: How the GM fills monster special feature answers.
PF1MK.Settings.DefaultRarity.Name: Default rarity
PF1MK.Settings.DefaultRarity.Hint: DC modifier: normal target = 10 + CR, common = 5 + CR, rare = 15 + CR.
PF1MK.Warn.NoTarget: Target exactly one token using Foundry's standard target tool.
PF1MK.Warn.NoGM: There is no active GM client available to calculate the target CR.
PF1MK.Warn.GMNoControlled: Control at least one monster token.
PF1MK.Warn.NotKnowledge: This message does not look like a Knowledge skill roll.
PF1MK.Warn.NoCR: Could not find the selected actor's CR.
PF1MK.Settings.GMRequestSound.Name: GM request sound
PF1MK.Settings.GMRequestSound.Hint: Plays a quiet standard notification only for the GM when a player sends a monster information request.
PF1MK.Settings.GMRequestSoundVolume.Name: GM request sound volume
PF1MK.Settings.GMRequestSoundVolume.Hint: Notification volume from 0 to 1. A value of 0 effectively mutes the sound.
